items.note: S3.1.1-S3.1.3 follow the proof at 741-765: the net change (JV+RG)x does not depend on the scratch values, the bit central coefficient is |S∩T| mod 2 and the side wires cancel it, and the three stages give (-y,x). The complex case's coefficient (|S∩T|-1)/2 and its neighbour rule are left out. So are h=100, the eight-row schedule (reduced to 'subtract-add-undo') and the wire counts.

The plan states D_out S D_in^{-1} and derives it as the paper does at 804-817: the stored array is D_v applied to the logical array, the edge applies D_vD_u^{-1}, and a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate. The per-route form ε_w D_sink D_source^{-1} is not written out, but the S3.2 and S3.4 motivations use it.

All of these are stated: nested nondegenerate labels built from triple indicator lines, the only decreasing edges being central 3->4 edges that each lose h, Ic such edges (so L=Ich), the sum Wm-2N+2L, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The derivation keeps the orthogonality fact (869) and the telescoping (1066-1071). It drops the label table (eq:motif-labels) and the edge-by-edge residual table (1022-1064), which are the substance of the proof, as well as the orthonormal-basis argument over F_2.

Projections as gate matrices, frames Φ_M, rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, one extra rank for each negative source projection, s_b=Wm-N+2L<Wm with deficit N-2L>0, and the endpoint difference P_{U^⊥}-(-P_U)=I_m. This is the proof at 1156-1171.

Phase frame C_U, weight additive mod 4 over orthogonal vectors, one kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=Wm-2N+2L<Wm, then diagonal corrections giving C^{⊗m} on every role. This follows 1231-1314. The k-column tensoring and the Z_{a,k} correction on the 27 support coordinates are compressed into 'diagonal corrections'.

Both halves of the saving are derived: s<Wm in both networks from L/N<1/2, through the deficits N-2L and 2N-2L. S3.6 states s/W<m^τ with τ=1-2^{-50} with no justification. The relative deficits η_b, η_c, the bound η>20·2^{-50} and log m<20 (1319-1338) are all missing.

The four elementary operations and the controlled shift and rational scaling are stated. The controlled-shift statement leaves out the conditions that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time and that the denominators be prime to q. S2.2.1 and S2.2.2 follow the proof of lem:ordered-affine-streams (577-604). The elementary-streams proof (513-550) and the negation step are not given.

Both lemmas are stated correctly. The shear-cost proof is reproduced faithfully: triangular factors by controlled shifts in descending order, the conjugation by E_2 and E_1^{-1}, and one interchange per one of Π through D_j+=H_i, swap, D_j=H_i-D_j. The elimination proof of the factorization itself (1375-1392) is only stated in S4.1.

Every step of the paper's proof is present: cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Φ_M frames giving H<-H+D on every row including scratch rows, the three shears, s recursive calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric sum O(e^τ), and the depth-first parking schedule with O(V) per node.

The plan covers the high-digit row field (cost O(Vρ)=O(V log u)), padding to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces handled by the power-width procedure with sum O(Ve^τ), and padding binary ranges to [q^e]. This is the paper's route. The unequal-width remark (1740-1762) is omitted.

Stated: the conjugation by P_M, one child per residual vector on the f axes of a slot, exactly s_c children, C^{⊗e} on every role, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. Missing: the identity (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z C^{⊗f} Z that makes every child a forward call (1883-1890), and the Gaussian-elimination count of row additions (1892-1901).

The derivation follows 2013-2114: eight conditional additions, each line a single cyclic shift with an offset independent of its target, the bad set B, the union bound giving δ_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, and T_0S_0^{-1} permuting only B. The lemma's time bound O(V(L^τ+1)+...) never appears in the plan.

The plan states the recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^τ+1) with leaves O(e), the internal-node overhead O(e^λ), and the λ' condition. Two steps are only named: how the rows are supplied (the first q_0 chunks taken as a row index and padded to a multiple of W^{k_0}, 2306-2323) and the leaf bound O(e^σ d^{β(1-σ)}) (2421-2430), which is where σ+β(1-σ) comes from.

Stated: D<=d chunks, an exact layer with one final truncation, O(Vd^{λ'}), guard width ⌈C_0d^{C_1}⌉=o(p), and error below √2·2^{-p} from absolute row sum one. Missing: the guard-width derivation through the arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E (2450-2586), and the check that the packed cost is uniform over the bands (2696-2735). K=⌊d^c⌋ appears only later, in S9.1.

Character cancellation by the y^{rj_0}=-1 shift, bit-reversed stored order, grouping into a parallel butterfly and a monomial, prefix-slot moves, chunk exchanges, simultaneous rounds, error √2ℓ2^{-p}, and the retained L(Bj) order, with the stated cost. All of it follows the paper.
Evaluation at base B_0=2^{4p}, four products with the established multiplier, |h_j|<B_0/2, centered recovery, reduction modulo y^r+1, and cost O(rp log(rp)). This matches 3233-3366.

Two forward transforms kept in LB order, pointwise products (the motivation states that the permutation commutes with them), the opposite transform scaled by M, error √2M(3ℓ+1)2^{-p}, and the stated cost. This is the paper's proof.

The one-dimensional identity P_sF_s=2^{2α^2}B_0P_tF_tA under θ>p/α^4, the Neumann inversion, two contractions, error p^2 and cost O(tp^{3/2+δ}α). The tensor form with γ=2dα^2, error dp^2 and the axis-exposure cost O(Tpd^2(1+ℓ^τ)) follow the paper. P_s and P_t are not defined explicitly.

Both identities are stated. The chirp a_j=exp(-πi Σ s_ij_i^2/t_i) is never defined. The cancellation of R is derived as in the paper (F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+, then the convolution rule). The Bluestein identity is only quoted; its coefficient computation (3938-3950) is not reproduced.

Present: the fixed exponents, b, p, d, K, T, r, t_i, the sizes, the prime windows with η=1/(4d), T/2<S<T, α^4θ_i>p, the deterministic search, and no wraparound. Absent: δ=1/16, α=⌈(12d^2b)^{1/4}⌉ and γ=2dα^2<=b/4, which the error bound relies on.

Φ: x->Πx_i^{μ_i} with μ_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i is an isomorphism. The triangular update b_i=a_i+μ_iΣa_jP_j is done in order d..1 by prefix-controlled shifts, with O(d^2) axis moves and cost O(Tpd^2(1+ℓ^τ)).

The exact twist is derived as at 4303-4347: well defined since (ζy)^r=1, the wrap factor ζ^r(-1)=1, and M_C=f*g/T a contraction. The computed version (4349-4413), with its approximate twist factors and the error each adds, is not covered.

The source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, 2^γ) with exact counterpart RF_s, the opposite-sign procedure by conjugation, and the six algorithm steps, including the two scales by S and their roles. The digit scaling by 2^{-b-2} is not mentioned.

The chain of error bounds (ring output below .701, chirp 8TL, E_s=9·2^γTL, (2E_s+2), E_w<28·2^γT^2L, final error below 1/2), the unique nearest integer, and the carry bound all follow the paper. The use of γ<=b/4 is implicit in the quoted 2^{-3b/4}.

The plan follows the paper's accounting: costs divided by V=Tp, the seven margins with minimum 2^{-181}=2κ, o(V) setup, polylog factors absorbed into p^κ, O(n(log n)^{1-κ}), and schoolbook below a cutoff. The individual margin formulas g_i are not listed.
S0 only refers to 'beating n log n' and relies on the nlogn-conjecture concept. The lower-bound formulation and the liminf negation are not stated.

errors.says: Run the bit network with each edge shear done by recursive interchanges, 'and finish with three shears'.
errors.paper: The interchange is three shears, D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D, and the network is the middle one; only the outer two are extra linear-cost shears.

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. It goes from the scalar exchange network to frames, labels and the rank budget, then the two interfaces with s<Wm, matrix-shear and the power-width recurrence for interchange, the phase-frame recursion and packed addition for the butterfly layer, and from there to transforms, convolution, resampling, CRT, exact recovery and time accounting. It thins out at three points. The label and residual tables behind Wm-2N+2L are asserted rather than derived. The exponent τ=1-2^{-50} is stated without the η>20·2^{-50}, log m<20 argument. The layer recurrence omits the leaf bound and the row-supply construction.

steps.note: The plan has a fixed scalar network on 3-subsets that sends (X,Y) to (-Y,X) and restores every scratch wire. It never gives h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3, m=h^3, or that the data pairs are indexed by triples of triples, so the defining quantities are missing.
There is a common invertible frame per gate, a pointwise gate commutes with it, the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, and only the edge changes D_vD_u^{-1} cost work.

Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from tensor products of triple indicator lines. Every edge joins comparable labels, and the only decreasing edges are the central 3->4 edges, each losing h. F^{⊗3} and its bilinear forms are not named explicitly.
S3.4.1 gives rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested U⊂V. The S3.4 method adds 'one extra rank per negative source projection', which is the N rank-one source exceptions.
The plan has the sum Wm-2N+2L, with Ic decreasing edges each of loss h (so L=Ich), and s_b=Wm-N+2L.
L/N is 100/539 and 101/539, both below 1/2, so the deficits N-2L and 2N-2L are positive and s<Wm.
The endpoint difference P_{U^⊥}-(-P_U)=I_m holds on every input role, so with frames Φ_M the network applies H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included.
A=E_1ΠE_2, and the shear costs exactly rank(A) interchanges plus O(V). The number of recursive calls is the sum of edge ranks, s.

The plan has children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^τ with τ=1-2^{-50}, and F_k=O(e^τ). The justification of τ (η>20·2^{-50}, log m<20) is missing. This is a borderline call: the recurrence and the exponent are present in their role in the chain.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs eight of the nine central steps: frames, labels, rank equal to dimension change, the budget, the strict saving L/N<1/2, the endpoint identity, edges as recursive calls, and the recurrence. The fixed network (C1) appears only structurally, without h=100, N or m. The numerical justification of τ=1-2^{-50} is also absent.
